references.text: Jesus sends out the seventy(-two) disciples, which is the background for why they now return with joy in verse 17.
Jesus gave the twelve disciples power and authority over all evil spirits, a parallel to how the seventy-two now experience that demons are subject to them.
Mark's account of the sending out of the twelve, where they among other things drove out many evil spirits – a parallel to the experience of the seventy-two.
Jesus promises that those who believe will drive out evil spirits in his name, which corresponds with the disciples' experience in Luke 10:17.
Paul drives out an evil spirit in the name of Jesus Christ, a concrete fulfillment of the authority experienced by the seventy-two disciples.
The account of the Jewish exorcists who tried to use Jesus' name to drive out evil spirits, which underscores the importance of the authority behind the name.
God has given Jesus the name above every name, so that every knee should bow – this confirms the authority inherent in Jesus' name and experienced by the disciples.
Jesus' immediate response to the disciples, where he confirms Satan's fall but reminds them that true joy should be that their names are written in heaven.
Philip drives out unclean spirits in Samaria, and there was great joy in that city – a parallel to the disciples' joy over the submission of demons.
A man who did not follow with the disciples drove out evil spirits in Jesus' name, showing that the power lay in Jesus' name, not in the person himself.
